case: Chowdury and Others v. Greece
decision: Bangladeshi strawberry pickers in Manolada were shot at when they asked for unpaid wages. The Court held that their work was forced labor and trafficking under Article 4, and that Greece failed to protect them and to punish those responsible.
norms_applied: European Convention on Human Rights; Forced Labor; Palermo; Trafficking

case: Workers of the Hacienda Brasil Verde v. Brazil
decision: 85 workers recruited from poor states were held in slavery on a cattle ranch in Pará. The first Inter-American judgment on slavery: Brazil was liable for failing to prevent it and for structural discrimination against poor rural workers.
norms_applied: American Convention on Human Rights, Art; Forced Labor; Slavery

case: Juridical Condition and Rights of Undocumented Migrants (Advisory Opinion OC-18/03)
decision: Once a migrant is employed, he or she has labor rights regardless of immigration status. Equality and non-discrimination are jus cogens, so states cannot condition labor rights on legal status.
norms_applied: American Convention on Human Rights, Art; Protection of the Rights of All Migrant Workers; Migrant Workers

case: Hoffman Plastic Compounds v. NLRB
forum: Supreme Court of the United States
decision: Undocumented workers unlawfully fired for union organizing cannot be awarded back pay. The ILO Committee on Freedom of Association later found this contrary to freedom of association (Case No. 2227).
norms_applied: National Labor Relations Act; Freedom of Association; Right to Organize

case: Cedar Point Nursery v. Hassid
forum: Supreme Court of the United States
decision: A California rule letting union organizers enter farms for limited hours to talk with farmworkers was held to be a taking of the growers' property, weakening farm organizing.
norms_applied: Agricultural Labor Relations Act; Right of Association (Agriculture)

case: Dunmore v. Ontario (Attorney General)
decision: Excluding farmworkers entirely from Ontario's labor relations law violated freedom of association under the Charter, because they could not organize without statutory protection.
norms_applied: Dunmore; Freedom of Association; Right of Association (Agriculture)

case: Ontario (Attorney General) v. Fraser
decision: Upheld Ontario's Agricultural Employees Protection Act, which lets farmworkers form associations without a duty on employers to bargain collectively.
norms_applied: Dunmore; Freedom of Association; Right of Association (Agriculture)

case: Siliadin v. France
decision: A Togolese girl made to work unpaid as a domestic servant was held in servitude. France breached Article 4 because its criminal law did not effectively punish servitude.
norms_applied: European Convention on Human Rights; Forced Labor; Slavery

case: Rantsev v. Cyprus and Russia
decision: Trafficking falls within Article 4. States must have laws against it, protect identified victims and investigate trafficking that crosses borders, including through 'artiste' visa schemes.
norms_applied: European Convention on Human Rights; Palermo; Trafficking

case: J. and Others v. Austria
decision: Filipino domestic workers trafficked by employers from the Gulf to Vienna. Austria had properly identified and supported them, and had no duty to prosecute acts committed abroad.
norms_applied: European Convention on Human Rights; Trafficking; Domestic Workers

case: Hirsi Jamaa and Others v. Italy
decision: Pushing migrants intercepted at sea back to Libya violated the prohibition of ill-treatment and of collective expulsion. Jurisdiction follows a state's control over people at sea.
norms_applied: European Convention on Human Rights; Refugee; non-refoulement

case: Khlaifia and Others v. Italy
forum: European Court of Human Rights (Grand Chamber)
decision: Holding Tunisian migrants in a reception center and on ships without a legal basis or review breached the right to liberty.
norms_applied: European Convention on Human Rights

case: Nadege Dorzema et al. v. Dominican Republic
decision: Soldiers fired on a truck carrying Haitian migrants and expelled the survivors collectively. Excessive force, arbitrary detention and discriminatory expulsion.
norms_applied: American Convention on Human Rights, Art

case: Rights and Guarantees of Children in the Context of Migration (Advisory Opinion OC-21/14)
decision: States may not detain children for migration reasons and must assess the best interests of the child before any return.
norms_applied: American Convention on Human Rights, Art; Rights of the Child

case: Bandhua Mukti Morcha v. Union of India
decision: Bonded laborers in stone quarries could bring a public interest petition. The state must identify, release and rehabilitate bonded laborers under the 1976 Act.
norms_applied: Bonded Labor; Forced Labor

case: People's Union for Democratic Rights v. Union of India
decision: Paying less than the minimum wage is 'forced labor' under Article 23 of the Constitution, because economic compulsion can force a person to work.
norms_applied: Forced Labor; Minimum Wage

case: Mahlangu v. Minister of Labour
decision: Excluding domestic workers from the injury compensation scheme was unconstitutional discrimination, and the ruling applied retroactively.
norms_applied: Domestic Workers

case: ILO Committee on Freedom of Association, Case No. 2704 (Canada)
forum: ILO Committee on Freedom of Association
decision: Asked the Government of Canada and Ontario to ensure that agricultural workers have the protection needed to bargain collectively.
norms_applied: Freedom of Association; Right of Association (Agriculture); Dunmore

case: Qatar: Article 26 complaint on forced labor of migrant workers
decision: A complaint on forced labor of migrant workers under the kafala system was closed in 2017 after Qatar agreed a technical cooperation program. It led to the 2020 reforms on changing employers and a minimum wage.
norms_applied: Forced Labor; Protection of Wages; Qatar

case: S.M. v. Croatia
forum: European Court of Human Rights (Grand Chamber)
decision: Forced prostitution is covered by Article 4, and the police must investigate credible trafficking claims thoroughly, including the coercion used.
norms_applied: European Convention on Human Rights; Trafficking

case: Union Interafricaine des Droits de l'Homme and Others v. Angola
forum: African Commission on Human and Peoples' Rights (Communication 159/96)
decision: Angola rounded up and expelled West African nationals in 1996, detaining them in poor conditions and seizing their property. The Commission held that mass expulsion of non-nationals is prohibited by the African Charter and that the deportees were denied the chance to challenge their removal before a court.
norms_applied: African Charter on Human and Peoples' Rights; Legal Regime of Foreign Citizens

case: Institute for Human Rights and Development in Africa v. Angola
forum: African Commission on Human and Peoples' Rights (Communication 292/04)
decision: Gambian nationals were arrested, held in overcrowded detention and expelled from Angola in 2004 without any chance to contest it. The Commission found violations of the rights to liberty, a fair hearing, property and protection against arbitrary and mass expulsion under the African Charter.
norms_applied: African Charter on Human and Peoples' Rights; Legal Regime of Foreign Citizens
